patterns.meaning: While it is still ~ / before ~ changes, (do something)

formation.form: 辞書形 / ている / ない形 + うちに
formation.example: 溶けないうちに・いるうちに

patterns.connection_notes: Noun + の + うちに / な-adj + な + うちに. Past tense (た形) is NOT used before うちに.
can_be_used_for: Doing something before a state changes
cannot_be_used_for: Past tense before うちに (×行ったうちに)
A state that will never change
patterns.exam_pinpoint: If the first half is a state that WILL CHANGE (明るい・若い・熱い・溶けない) and the second half is a deliberate action → うちに

confusable_with.difference: 間に just marks a time span; うちに(A) stresses 'before the state changes, take the chance'.
confusable_with.how_to_choose: If losing the chance is implied (溶けない・暗くならない) → うちに.

confusable_with.difference: 前に is a plain time order; ないうちに adds 'before the bad change happens'.
confusable_with.how_to_choose: Negative + うちに when the change is undesirable.

common_traps: た形 + うちに is always wrong
Using うちに with an unchanging fact (日本人のうちに ×)

examples.japanese: 日本{にほん}にいるうちに一度{いちど}富士山{ふじさん}に登{のぼ}ってみたい。
examples.english: While I'm still in Japan, I want to climb Mt. Fuji once.
examples.note: Being in Japan will end → do it before it changes (will: ～たい).

examples.japanese: 溶{と}けないうちに早{はや}く食{た}べてくださいね。
examples.english: Please eat it quickly before it melts.
examples.note: ないうちに = before the undesirable change; request is OK.

more_examples.japanese: 明{あか}るいうちに庭{にわ}の掃除{そうじ}をしてしまおう。
more_examples.english: Let's finish cleaning the garden while it's still light.

patterns.book_explanation: 「～の状態が変わる前に、…する。」～ is the state before the change; … is a deliberate (intentional) action.
patterns.one_line_memory_trick: うちに(A) = 'while the window is open, jump through it.'

patterns.meaning: While ~ was going on, (something changed without my intent)

formation.form: 辞書形 / ている / ない形 + うちに
formation.example: 聞いているうちに・重ねるうちに

patterns.connection_notes: Mainly verbs of continuous action (～ている・～ているうちに). The second half is a CHANGE (～なる・～てしまった・～ようになる).
can_be_used_for: Unplanned change during an ongoing action
Gradual change (～ようになる・～てきた)
cannot_be_used_for: Speaker's will / intention in the second half
Non-change states in the second half
patterns.exam_pinpoint: If the second half is an UNINTENDED CHANGE (眠ってしまった・～ようになった・暗くなっていた) → ているうちに

confusable_with.difference: 間に can take an intentional one-time action; うちに(B) takes a natural change.
confusable_with.how_to_choose: Change without will (眠る・なる) → うちに; deliberate action at one point → 間に.

common_traps: Option with ～よう / ～つもり after うちに(B) is wrong — the change is not intentional

examples.japanese: 音楽{おんがく}を聞{き}いているうちに眠{ねむ}ってしまった。
examples.english: I fell asleep while listening to music.
examples.note: Falling asleep = unintended change → うちに(B).

examples.japanese: 気{き}がつかないうちに外{そと}^は暗{くら}くなっていた。
examples.english: Before I noticed, it had gotten dark outside.
examples.note: Natural change without the speaker's will.

more_examples.japanese: 少{すこ}し難{むずか}しい曲{きょく}でも、練習{れんしゅう}を重{かさ}ねるうちに弾{ひ}けるようになりますよ。
more_examples.english: Even a slightly difficult piece—you'll be able to play it as you keep practicing.

patterns.book_explanation: 「～の状態が続いているときに、…に変わる。」～ is continuous; … is a change not controlled by the speaker.
patterns.one_line_memory_trick: うちに(B) = 'while I was busy… oops, it changed.'

patterns.meaning: 間: during the whole time ~ / 間に: at some point during ~

formation.form: 辞書形 / ている / ない形 + 間・間に

patterns.connection_notes: 間 (no に) → second half is CONTINUOUS (ずっと～ていた). 間に → second half is a ONE-TIME action or change.
can_be_used_for: 間: something continuing for the whole period
間に: a single event within the period
Requests (留守の間、～お願いできませんか)
cannot_be_used_for: 間 + one-time action (×間、出かけた)
間に + continuous state (×間に、ずっと見ていた)
patterns.exam_pinpoint: Second half continuous (ずっと・～ていた) → 間 / second half a single event (出かけた・生えた) → 間に

confusable_with.difference: うちに has the nuance 'before it changes' or 'unintended change'; 間に is neutral time span.
confusable_with.how_to_choose: Look for a state that will change/chance-taking → うちに; neutral span → 間に.

common_traps: Choosing 間に when the main clause is ずっと～ていた (should be 間)
Choosing 間 when the main clause is a one-off action

examples.japanese: お母{かあ}さんが昼寝{ひるね}をしている間{あいだ}、子{こ}どもたち^はテレビを見{み}ていた。
examples.english: While mother napped, the children watched TV (the whole time).

examples.japanese: お母{かあ}さんが昼寝{ひるね}をしている間{あいだ}に、子{こ}どもたち^は遊{あそ}びに出{で}かけた。
examples.english: While mother was napping, the children went out to play.
examples.note: One-time action (出かけた) → 間に.

more_examples.japanese: わたしが旅行{りょこう}で留守{るす}の間{あいだ}、うちの犬{いぬ}の世話{せわ}をお願{ねが}いできないでしょうか。
more_examples.english: Could I ask you to look after my dog while I'm away on a trip?

more_examples.japanese: わたしが旅行{りょこう}で留守{るす}の間{あいだ}に、庭{にわ}に草{くさ}がたくさん生{は}えてしまった。
more_examples.english: While I was away on a trip, lots of weeds grew in the garden.

patterns.book_explanation: 間: ～ continuous, … also continuous. 間に: ～ continuous, … is a momentary action or change.
patterns.one_line_memory_trick: 間 = a long line; 間に = a dot on that line.

patterns.pattern: ～てからでないと… / ～てからでなければ…
patterns.reading: てからでないと / てからでなければ
patterns.meaning: Unless/until ~ is done first, … can't happen

formation.form: て形 + からでないと / からでなければ
formation.example: 相談してからでないと

patterns.connection_notes: Only verb て形. Second half must be NEGATIVE / impossible (～できない・～てはいけない・無理だ).
can_be_used_for: Prohibition until a condition is met
patterns.exam_pinpoint: If the second half is negative/impossible (決められない・いけない・無理だ) and the first half is a prerequisite → てからでないと

confusable_with.difference: てから just orders events; てからでないと says the second thing is impossible without the first.
confusable_with.how_to_choose: Negative/impossible ending → てからでないと.

common_traps: Option with a positive ending (～できる) after てからでないと is wrong

examples.japanese: 運転免許{うんてんめんきょ}を取{と}ってからでなければ車{くるま}を運転{うんてん}してはいけない。
examples.english: You must not drive until you have a license.

examples.japanese: 病気{びょうき}が治{なお}ってからでなければ激{はげ}しい運動{うんどう}^は無理{むり}だ。
examples.english: Hard exercise is impossible until you recover.

more_examples.japanese: 高{たか}い物{もの}なので、家族{かぞく}と相談{そうだん}してからでないと買{か}うかどうか決{き}められませんね。
more_examples.english: It's expensive, so I can't decide whether to buy it until I talk with my family.

patterns.book_explanation: 「～の前は…の状態が続く。」… expresses a negative meaning or minus state.
patterns.one_line_memory_trick: てからでないと = 'Not before ~. No way.'

patterns.reading: ところだ / ところを・ところで・ところへ
patterns.meaning: Just about to ~ / in the middle of ~ / just finished ~
patterns.connection_notes: The particle changes with the following verb: ～ところを見つかる/注意される, ～ところで(電話が鳴った), ～ところへ(帰ってきた).
cannot_be_used_for: Long-past events (×去年食べたところだ)
patterns.exam_pinpoint: Choose the particle by the next verb: 見る/注意する/見つかる → ところを; 鳴る/始まる(interrupt) → ところで; 来る/帰る → ところへ

confusable_with.difference: たところ = moment right after (objectively); たばかり = subjectively 'only a short time ago' (can be days).
confusable_with.how_to_choose: Weeks/days ago with 'still new' feeling → たばかり.

common_traps: Using ところへ with a verb that isn't movement/arrival
Wrong tense before ところ (辞書形 vs た形)

examples.japanese: 試験中{しけんちゅう}、となりの人{ひと}の答{こた}えを見{み}ているところを先生{せんせい}に注意{ちゅうい}された。
examples.english: During the exam, I was warned by the teacher while looking at my neighbor's answers.
examples.note: Caught in the act → ているところを.

examples.japanese: ケーキができ上{あ}がったところへ子{こ}どもたちが帰{かえ}ってきた。
examples.english: The kids came home just as the cake was ready.
examples.note: Arrival verb 帰ってきた → ところへ.

more_examples.japanese: ロケット^は間{ま}もなく飛{と}び立{た}つところです。
more_examples.english: The rocket is about to take off.

more_examples.japanese: 楽{たの}しみにしていたテレビドラマが始{はじ}まったところで電話{でんわ}が鳴{な}った。
more_examples.english: The phone rang just as the drama I'd been looking forward to started.

patterns.book_explanation: 「～の直前だ・進行中だ・直後だ。」In a sentence, the particle after ところ (を・で・へ) depends on the verb that follows.
patterns.one_line_memory_trick: ところ = a camera snapshot: before / during / after.
